clinical_category: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control

semantic_correction.stem: A hospitalized client with confirmed C. difficile infection has had no diarrhea since this morning. A plan is entered to discontinue Contact Precautions now. Which action should the nurse take?

options.A: Clarify the plan because CDC recommends continuing Contact Precautions for at least 48 hours after diarrhea resolves.
options.B: Discontinue precautions now because the absence of diarrhea for several hours meets the CDC duration recommendation.
options.C: Continue Contact Precautions permanently because a history of C. difficile requires lifelong isolation.
options.D: Limit Contact Precautions to toileting because environmental contamination is not relevant once diarrhea stops.

semantic_correction.rationale: CDC's May 13, 2026 acute-care guidance recommends maintaining Contact Precautions for confirmed C. difficile infection for at least 48 hours after diarrhea has resolved; facilities may continue precautions longer, up to the duration of hospitalization. A client whose diarrhea stopped only this morning has not met the minimum CDC duration. C. difficile also requires environmental cleaning and dedicated equipment, so precautions are not limited to toileting encounters.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: For confirmed C. difficile infection, continue Contact Precautions for at least 48 hours after diarrhea resolves and recognize that facilities may extend precautions through hospitalization.
semantic_correction.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
semantic_correction.source_document_title: Clinical Guidance for C. diff Infection Prevention in Acute Care Facilities
semantic_correction.source_locator: Isolate and initiate contact precautions — confirmed CDI: maintain Contact Precautions for at least 48 hours after diarrhea has resolved, or longer, up to the duration of hospitalization; Perform environmental cleaning — daily sporicidal cleaning and dedicated equipment practices
semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: For confirmed CDI, CDC recommends maintaining Contact Precautions for at least 48 hours after diarrhea resolves, with longer continuation up to the duration of hospitalization as appropriate.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: shortened the uniquely long correct answer, removed the 'only' distractor pattern, and centered the item on CDC's updated May 13, 2026 minimum 48-hour post-diarrhea Contact Precautions duration.

audit_findings_append.finding: The original concept was current but structurally cued by a very long answer and an absolute distractor. The revised item retains the exact 2026 CDC duration rule with balanced alternatives.

option_audit.A: Correct. The client has not yet completed the CDC minimum 48-hour period after diarrhea resolution.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Several hours without diarrhea does not meet the minimum 48-hour recommendation.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. CDC does not recommend lifelong Contact Precautions solely because of prior CDI.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. C. difficile precautions address broader contact and environmental transmission risk, not toileting alone.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone applies the current CDC duration recommendation to the timeline in the stem.
cueing_check: All four choices are precaution-management actions of comparable length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.
